title: Dal Tadka

ingredients.title: For the Dal
items: Toor dal (split pigeon peas) – 1 cup (200 g)
Masoor dal (red lentils) – ¼ cup (50 g), optional

ingredients.title: For the Tadka
items: Ghee – 3 tbsp (or vegetable oil for vegan preparation)
Garlic – 6–8 cloves, finely chopped or crushed
Kasuri methi – 1 tsp, lightly roasted and crushed

ingredients.title: For the Finishing Tadka
items: Kashmiri red chili powder – ½ tsp

instruction.title: Cook the Dal
steps: Rinse the toor dal and optional masoor dal together until the water runs mostly clear.
Combine the dals, turmeric, salt, and water in a pressure cooker or heavy-bottomed pot.
Pressure cook for 3–4 whistles over medium heat, or simmer in a pot until the lentils are completely soft and mushy.
Mash the cooked dal lightly with the back of a ladle until creamy.
Keep the cooked dal aside.

instruction.title: Prepare the First Tadka
steps: Heat 3 tbsp ghee in a deep pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and mustard seeds and allow them to crackle.
Add dried red chilies and hing and sauté briefly.
Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent.
Add garlic, ginger, and green chilies and cook until lightly golden and fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and the oil begins to separate.
Add red chili powder, coriander powder, and garam masala.
Stir well and cook briefly to bloom the spices.

instruction.title: Combine & Simmer
steps: Add the cooked dal to the prepared tadka.
Add water as needed to reach a smooth, pourable consistency.
Mix thoroughly and simmer for 5–7 minutes over low heat.
Taste and adjust salt and spices as needed.

instruction.title: Prepare the Finishing Tadka
steps: Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a small pan.
Add sliced garlic and sauté until golden brown.
Turn off the heat and immediately stir in Kashmiri red chili powder.
Pour the hot finishing tadka directly over the simmering dal.

instruction.title: Finish & Serve
steps: Sprinkle roasted and crushed kasuri methi over the dal.
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot with steamed basmati rice, jeera rice, or butter naan.
Accompany with onion salad and lemon wedges.

chefTips: Dal texture: Mash the cooked lentils lightly for a creamy consistency while retaining some texture.
Kasuri methi: Lightly roast the dried fenugreek leaves before crushing to intensify their aroma.
Chili powder: Kashmiri red chili powder gives the finishing tadka a vibrant red color without excessive heat.
Ghee: Using ghee in both tadkas provides the characteristic rich, buttery aroma of restaurant-style dal.
Consistency: Dal thickens as it sits, so adjust with hot water immediately before serving if needed.
Dhaba-style flavor: For a smoky finish, use the dhungar method with a hot charcoal piece, a little ghee, and a covered pot for about 2 minutes.
